original.evidence: Plans/Models_System.md:9821–9896 gives two populated JSON records. Example 1 is “the run's own pick is honored”. Example 2 contains “"requested_model_id": "gpt-5.2-codex"”, “"resolved_model_id": "gpt-5.5-codex"”, “"fallback_used": true” and “"clamp_reason": "effort_clamped"”. Both include the shared requested/effective, account, role and selection fields from lines 84–96 as well as visibility. I parsed both JSON objects.

Plans/chain-wizard-flexibility.md:28–34 identifies “Historical intent-based workflow definitions retained for source-lineage compatibility.” DL-472 moves the active targeted-revision contract to PRDB-014. Plans/PRD_Builder.md:841–1214 supplies Draft 2020-12 schemas in which “`operation` selects exactly one payload schema” for comment, replace, insert_after and remove. An invalid input “gets `outcome = cannot_apply` with `failure_code = payload_invalid` and is not sent to the model”. I checked the embedded schema, one valid payload of each operation and rejection of unknown payload keys. The old generation-suggestion trigger is historical.

Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:322 says the six uppercase strings are “the only `disabled_reason` values a `capabilities.get` response carries”. Lines 6705–6720 identify all ten lowercase inputs as route-row values and supply the conversion, including “`BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED` when the unverified route belongs to the active backend” and “`NOT_CONFIGURED` otherwise”. “`RATE_LIMITED` has no route row value”. §1.4 determines the one emitted reason when causes coincide. Lines 1011–1013 explicitly translate the two AC-MED05 labels into the six-value wire vocabulary.

Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:712 says the lookaround forms are “kept as source lineage and as the behaviour reference only” and mandates the two replacements at 716 and 720. Prompt cleaning preserves the consumed boundary: “never the `model_end` text” (714). Appendix A expressly sends readers to “the canonical lookaround-free matchers” in §3.4 (1102), and MGAC-043 identifies the old forms as lineage. I ran both new expressions with the Rust regex engine on “use blue mark for @other-id” and obtained the same two captures as the historical matchers.

original.evidence: Plans/usage-feature.md:772–776 and 803 point to the named hostability section, WS-017/019 for grid and gestures and “section=3. Layout persistence”. Line 823 binds “`configuration_refs`” to WS-020 and the configuration record to WS-004. At 851 the Dashboard add-widget flow resolves to “`Plans/Widget_System.md#WS-030`, Catalogue”. Plans/Widget_System.md:1219 independently maps the old §§2/3/4/7 and #5 and distinguishes these uses from the actual §4 Progress catalog.

Plans/DRY_Rules.md:204–241 provides executable normalization and comparison definitions, nine vectors, and the explicit reference “`scripts/pm-packet-fidelity-match.py` implements this comparison”. I read the script at the assigned commit. Lines 13–30 remove standalone ContractRef lines, normalize line endings and horizontal whitespace, collapse excess blank lines, reject an empty packet, then “return p in normalize(target)”. Running its --self-test printed “9/9 vectors pass” and exited 0. Line 241 separately identifies lint-contractrefs as a spelling/path check.

regressions.what: For synthetic invalid UTF-8 input the reference CLI raises UnicodeDecodeError and exits 1. §7.1 advertises 1 for no match and 2 for a read error. An undecodable packet is reported to callers as a legitimate comparison miss. I reproduced this in memory with a single 0xFF byte.

original.evidence: Plans/Widget_System.md:1221 explicitly resolves both external references: “`§7` resolves to `## 3. Layout persistence` with WS-020 (`configuration_refs`) and WS-004 (configuration record).” It identifies the separate “`### Progress-only widget hostability`” and “`### Catalog source and drill linkage`” headings. Plans/usage-feature.md:823 uses the live configuration anchors and retires its numeric alias. The preserved FinalGUISpec Appendix C #7 reference is separately identified as a dashboard key migration and mapped to layout persistence at Widget_System.md:1219–1221.

Plans/Widget_System.md:114–127 lists `progress.blocked-concerns` among the thirteen entries. The parsed JSON at 140–157 names “"widget_id": "progress.blocked-concerns"”, “"host_surface": "orchestrator:progress"” and “"data_ref": "projection.progress.blocked-concerns"”. It supplies identity, scope, filter, sort, display, drill target, refresh and empty state. Lines 160–167 explain those WS-006 shell fields. Line 1223 explicitly supersedes the dashboard sample for this finding.

Plans/FinalGUISpec.md:4393 binds disclosure to “`skipped_persona_controls[]`” with “`control`, `requested_value`, `effective_value?`, `outcome = skipped | clamped`, `provider`, `reason`” and says the inline and history views “read the same persisted entries”. Lines 4405–4409 and F3-296 bind the four Builder settings to “`cmd.settings.transaction.preview` / `cmd.settings.transaction.apply`”, preserve the two named crew settings and protected overseer, and retire the Interview-stage, node/package/lane/seam, Multi-Pass and per-mapping model editors as DL-2602 specifies. The retained settings have inventory entries.

Plans/FinalGUISpec.md:28998 says “`Refresh Models` and `Retry check` both dispatch `cmd.model.refresh`”. Retry supplies “`refresh_reason = free_models_update_retry` and no `provider_id`”; View details opens the existing activation, quarantine and rollback records locally. Lines 29062 and 29072 say “`Use for a job` writes exactly one Default models job row through `cmd.settings.transaction.preview` / `cmd.settings.transaction.apply`”. MS-120 and DL-2603 retire the ranked editor and store. The job settings are present in settings_inventory and the catalog defines the refresh result and `model.catalog_refreshed` at Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:8689.

Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:625–630,663 makes `cmd.docker.build` a compatibility alias and registers `cmd.docker.build.image` as a concrete mode. Lines 12725–12728 now register “`cmd.github.actions.settings.open` | Open Actions Settings” and the Current Branch command as GI-008 subview navigation. The previously unmatched Actions tokens get individual dispositions: show aliases panel switch, switch_subview is the three-view compatibility row, and open_run_diff aliases open_related_diff. The production matrix contains “handlers::github::actions_settings_open” and the no-persist navigation contract.
